newsitem.title: GERMANY: German minister says to cull British, Swiss cattle.
newsitem.headline: German minister says to cull British, Swiss cattle.

text.p: A senior German Agriculture Ministry official said on Wednesday all cattle imported from Britain and Switzerland would be culled to calm public fears after a case of mad cow disease in a Germany.
The state secretary at the ministry Franz-Josef Feiter told a news conference the decision would affect 2,600 cattle from Britain and a further 2,600 from Switzerland.
Feiter was speaking after a meeting in Bonn with officials from Germany's 16 regional states a day after the ministry said a Galloway cow, of a British mother, had been infected with mad cow disease.

"The offspring of British and Swiss cattle will be placed under observation until officials ascertain whether the latest case definitely involved a German-born cow," Feiter said. "There is some doubt about the precise origin of the cow in the present case."
He said there were about 14,000 offspring from the 5,200 British and Swiss cattle due to be slaughtered.
The cow in question died in December last year but the Agriculture Ministry said only on Tuesday that tests had proved it was infected with bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) or mad cow disease.
